migration_example.reason: A later ctl-meta session defined an upstream subject profile.

append_only_correction_model.principle: Do not mutate a subject in place. Admit a new subject revision or subject operation object.

redirect_example.reason: SU(2) itself is a Lie group; SU(2)_k is the modular tensor category family.

split_example.reason: The original subject conflated a person, a paper, and a link family.

current_view_rules.alias_rule: Alias collisions should produce disambiguation rather than silent winner-takes-all resolution.
current_view_rules.claim_precision_rule: A claim may cite a broad subject for discoverability, but it should also cite the most precise known subject for the asserted computation or theorem.
current_view_rules.deprecated_subject_rule: Deprecated subjects should not be used as primary about/uses targets in new claims unless the edge role is historical or redirected_from.
current_view_rules.projection: A current subject view is derived by replaying admitted subject definitions and operations from the CTL current root.
current_view_rules.redirect_rule: Redirect chains should be resolved in generated views. Redirect cycles are invalid.

future_verifier_rules: Verify subject object CIDs through the ordinary CTL object store.
Verify subject revision updates parent the previous active revision for the same logical id.
Reject redirect cycles in the projected current view.
Warn or fail on alias collisions without an admitted disambiguation subject.
Warn or fail when new primary edges target deprecated subjects.
Require explicit reasons for split, merge, redirect, deprecate, and subject_kind correction operations.
Require migration operations to preserve old subject ids as redirected_from or historical edges.

ctl_kernel_role: Revision envelopes, parents, roots, policy, and admission transitions.
No knowledge of research topics, wiki pages, Yasui links, MTCs, or mathematical proof criteria.
downstream_subject_layer_role: Define project-local subject identities, aliases, display names, scope notes, status, edges, and correction operations.
Provide machine-readable material from which human wiki views can be generated.
Make split, merge, redirect, deprecation, and correction append-only CTL records.
generated_wiki_role: Render human-readable pages or search results from admitted subject definitions, subject edges, and subject operations.
Never become the normative record itself.
May be regenerated after subject splits, redirects, or ontology migrations.

problem_statement.core_principle: Subjects may be provisional; admitted claims and artifacts must not be ambiguous about what they actually assert or compute.
motivation: Research projects need durable search handles for people, papers, figures, links, categories, experiments, claims, methods, and artifacts.
Agents may choose the wrong granularity, for example conflating a person named Yasui with one Yasui paper or conflating the Lie group SU(2) with the modular tensor categories SU(2)_k.
The system must make wrong granularity cheap to repair without silently mutating old objects.
The same subject may need to be referenced across future CTL wiki views or across projects, while external URLs may rot.
non_goals: Do not add subject semantics to CTL Kernel.
Do not define twisted-yetter mathematical ontology as an upstream ResearchCTL requirement.
Do not make prose wiki pages normative.
Do not require a perfect ontology before recording useful subject objects.

proposed_profiles.purpose: Define or revise one subject identity under a logical id.
Attach a subject to another subject, claim, artifact, reference, experiment, method, or generated view with an explicit role.
Record append-only corrections to the subject graph.

scope.claim_boundary: This is a twisted-yetter downstream design proposal. It is not a CTL Meta specification, not a ResearchCTL upstream profile, and not yet enforced by dedicated subject-layer verifier rules.
scope.migration_expectation: A future ctl-meta session may copy, revise, reject, or replace this proposal. If ctl-meta later defines a different subject profile, twisted-yetter should migrate by admitting explicit mapping and migration objects rather than rewriting these records.
scope.question: Specify a downstream subject layer for future CTL-style search, disambiguation, correction, and generated wiki views.
scope.source_of_truth_policy: The normative record is this admitted JSON payload and its CTL revision object. Any future human-facing wiki page must be generated from admitted subject objects and edges, not treated as the source of truth.

identity_vs_locator: External URLs, arXiv links, DOIs, and file paths are locators or references, not subject identity.
Important external sources should have local reference records, capture times, and hashes when possible.
Locator-only subjects or references should be marked with rot risk.
subject_id_policy: Subject ids should be stable logical identifiers, not display names.
Subject ids should include project or namespace prefix when intended for cross-project citation.
Display names and aliases may change through append-only revisions or operations.
A broad or ambiguous subject may remain as a hub after finer subjects are split out.
subject_kind_policy: subject_kind should be typed but project-local kinds are allowed.
Changing subject_kind in the current view should require an explicit correction operation.
A subject_kind correction does not erase prior mistaken revisions.

terminology.rationale: The word wiki suggests editable prose pages. The desired source of truth is a machine-readable subject graph; wiki pages are only generated views.

payload.title: Downstream subject layer design proposal v0

upstream_feedback_notes.expected_future_ctl_meta_work: A separate ctl-meta session should review this downstream proposal and decide whether to define a generic ResearchCTL subject profile. That session may reuse this design or replace it with a different upstream model.
why_this_may_be_generically_useful: Any ResearchCTL project with long-lived notes will need subject disambiguation and repair.
Append-only subject correction fits CTL's existing revision model.
Generated wiki views are a natural consumer of admitted subject graphs.
why_this_should_not_be_kernel: Subject meanings are research ontology, not CTL object semantics.
Kernel validators should not need to know what a paper, theorem, MTC, or link is.
Projects should be free to define domain-specific subject kinds downstream.
